title: Threshold Endurance Run with Strength Maintenance

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move slowly through full range, sync with breath. Warm up the spine and engage core.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Extend opposite arm and leg fully, maintain neutral spine. Focus on control, not speed.

items.name: Light Jogging
items.cues: Easy conversational pace to elevate heart rate gradually. Build up to workout intensity.

items.name: Threshold Run
items.cues: Run at a pace you could sustain for about an hour. RPE 7-8: challenging but controlled breathing. This is race-pace effort for the 45km Engelbrektsloppet. Maintain steady effort throughout.

items.name: Back Squat
items.cues: Heavy load, explosive concentric. Maintain upright torso, knees track over toes. Drive through heels.

items.name: Bent Over Row
items.cues: Heavy compound pull. Keep back flat, chest up. Retract scapula and drive elbows back powerfully.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Controlled hip mobility work. Open hips gently, maintain upright posture. Breathe through each rep.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Hold each side 45 seconds. Lean into stretch, keep heel down. Release running tension in calves.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Hold 30 seconds each side. Place palm on wall, lean forward gently. Stretch chest and anterior shoulder.

items.name: Deep Breathing
items.cues: Slow diaphragmatic breathing. Inhale for 4 counts, exhale for 4 counts. Activate parasympathetic nervous system.

rationale: With 5 days until the 45km Engelbrektsloppet race, this threshold workout develops race-specific aerobic capacity at RPE 7-8, matching the intensity needed for sustained ultra-distance performance.

Extended running workload (40 min threshold) directly prepares for the race duration and effort level. Strength maintenance with Back Squats and Rows preserves power and running economy without compromising recovery.
16 days since last recorded workout warrants a comprehensive session; advanced fitness level supports this higher volume and intensity to consolidate training gains just before the race.
